messages.subject: Error "Infinite values were detected in model variables: logProb..."
parts:
Hi nimble users,

I am a beginner in Nimble. I did a few models but I am facing an error now. I hope you can help me to solve it. 
I am doing a CJS model with multiple states and there also exists uncertainties in assigning states. I attached my R code here and also a trial data which I am using to test my model. 
The model was running without any problem until I incorporated more states. The initial error I am getting is 
[Note] Infinite values were detected in model variables: logProb_alive, logProb_mydata.
And, then after compiling I am also getting a lot of lines of error,
.....
warning: problem initializing stochastic node alive[1, 2]: logProb is -Inf. warning: problem initializing stochastic node alive[2, 2]: logProb is -Inf. warning: problem initializing stochastic node alive[5, 7]: logProb is -Inf. warning: problem initializing stochastic node alive[7, 6]: logProb is -Inf. warning: problem initializing stochastic node alive[9, 2]: logProb is -Inf. warning: logProb of data node mydata[3, 1]: logProb is -Inf. warning: logProb of data node mydata[4, 2]: logProb is -Inf. warning: logProb of data node mydata[9, 1]: logProb is -Inf. warning: problem initializing stochastic node alive[4, 4]: logProb is -Inf. warning: problem initializing stochastic node alive[8, 4]: logProb is -Inf. warning: problem initializing stochastic node alive[1, 4]: logProb is -Inf. warning: logProb of data node mydata[2, 3]: logProb is -Inf. 
....... 
I thought the problem was arising from initializing, so I tried different ways. But, I am still getting the same errors. It would be great if anyone has any ideas on how can I fix this problem or if I am doing any mistakes in my code.

messages.author: f116cbe5c604c988
messages.subject: Re: Error "Infinite values were detected in model variables: logProb..."
parts:
Arjun, I hope that a quick and short answer to get you started it helpful, and I'm not able to give a longer explanation right now.

This comes down to model initialization.  At least your 'alive' variable is not properly initialized, and the MCMC cannot recover.  You will need to modify your initial values list, to make it so that the model is fully initialized.  An easy way to check that is when Rmodel$calculate() returns a real (usually negative) number.

Here was my quick look at your model, along with some comments:


Rmodel <- nimbleModel(multievent_code, my.constants, my.data, initial.values)   ## create model

Rmodel$calculate()   ## returns -Inf

## NB: next feature is undocumented and comes with no guarantees, and sometimes gives an error
Rmodel$initializeInfo(TRUE)   ## see where it's coming from:  the alive variable

Rmodel$logProb_alive   ## look at logProbs for alive.  the [2,4] is one -Inf entry

i <- 2
j <- 4

Rmodel$logProb_alive[i,j]   ## -Inf
Rmodel$alive[i,j]   ## here's the value being provided by the inits list: 1
Rmodel$alive[i,j-1]     ## here's the previous value: 2
Rmodel$px[Rmodel$alive[i,j-1],1:5]    ## the categorical prior for alive[i,j] gives 0 probability for the value of 1

In short, you'll have to modify the initial values for 'alive' at the very least, so that Rmodel$calculate() gives a real number.

I hope this helps get you started.

messages.author: d78486bfff620d81
messages.subject: Re: Error "Infinite values were detected in model variables: logProb..."
parts:
Hi Arjun, it looks like you have some inconsistencies in your initialization that cause the -Inf when you calculate the model log probabilities.

> Rmodel$calculate('alive[7,3]')
[1] -Inf
> Rmodel$alive[7,]
Fall_2009 Fall_2010 Fall_2011 Fall_2012 Fall_2013 Fall_2014 Fall_2015
        0         5         1         1         1         1         1
> Rmodel$alive[7,3]
Fall_2011
        1 
> my.constants$First[7]
[1] 2
> Rmodel$alive[7,2]
Fall_2010
        5
> Rmodel$gamma[5,1:5]
[1] 0 0 0 0 1

The model specification for 'alive[7,3]' has `dcat(gamma[alive[i,j-1],1:5])`, but that set of gamma values (based on 'alive[7,2]'), puts 0 probability that 'alive[7,3]' takes the value of '1', which is its initial value.

-Chris
